title: Fully Confidential Ethereum Transactions — Aztec Network
quote: Note-based system rather than account balances; join-split transactions validating A + B = C + D through ZK proofs. Private execution computed locally by users; public execution processed by sequencers. Note Tree contains all notes ever created; Nullifier Tree records destroyed notes. Merkle roots published to Ethereum L1.

title: Aztec Network — homepage
quote: The first decentralized, privacy-preserving L2 on Ethereum.

title: Getting to Know Aztec's Privacy-First Ethereum L2 — Bankless
quote: Noir, a Rust-like language; Private Execution Environment (PXE) handles client-side computation, key management, proof generation; Aztec Virtual Machine (AVM) runs public functions on sequencers. The EVM's transparent queryable state makes privacy essentially impossible without compromising security.

title: Aztec Network's $61M Community TGE and Noir 1.0 — BlockEden
quote: February 2026 community-first token sale raising $61 million from 16,700+ participants, and Noir 1.0 pre-release. Alpha Network launched 31 March 2026. On 17 March 2026 the team discovered a critical vulnerability in the Aztec proving system; v5 fix planned for July 2026.

title: Aztec Launches Alpha Network — The Defiant
quote: Ethereum's first L2 for private smart contracts.

title: Polygon Miden Deep Dive — Obscura
quote: Actor Model where each account is an independent state machine. Notes are asynchronous messages between actors. Notes come in two varieties: public (full content on-chain) and private (only the hash on-chain). Accounts in Sparse Merkle Trees; notes in Merkle Mountain Ranges; nullifiers in Sparse Merkle Trees. Miden recursively aggregates transaction proofs into batches, then blocks, before settlement on Ethereum.

title: Technical Analysis of Transactions in Miden — HackMD
quote: Each transaction generates new notes as outputs. The script is executed as part of the transaction with the results included in the transaction proof. Clients execute transactions locally and generate corresponding ZKPs. STARK proofs validate transactions without revealing sensitive data contents.

title: Miden — homepage
quote: Pioneering ZK architecture enabling local and private transaction execution. Recursive proof capability. Post-quantum cryptography.

title: Polygon Miden Alpha Testnet v2 — Polygon Blog
quote: STARK-based zk-rollup with client-side proving; users locally generate proofs for their own state transitions without disclosing state to the network.

title: Railgun vs Aztec — Railgun Project
quote: Railgun is a system of smart contracts deployed on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Polygon that uses ZK-proofs to shield tokens within pools, allowing users to swap, lend, and provide liquidity without unshielding assets.

title: Aztec vs Railgun: 2026 DeFi Privacy and Fees Comparison — Baltex
quote: Railgun charges a flat 0.25% fee for shielding/unshielding plus Relayer Fees (often a 10% premium over current gas prices). Aztec internal transfers under $0.10; bridging from L1 costs $5.00 to $15.00. Railgun's Private Proof of Innocence (PPOI) cryptographically proves funds don't originate from blacklisted addresses without revealing identity or transaction history.

title: Railgun vs Aztec — Chainscore Labs
quote: Railgun is an EVM privacy SDK; Aztec is a zk-Rollup. Different deployment shapes.

title: zkEVM comparison — Polygon zkEVM vs zkSync Era vs Linea vs Scroll vs Taiko — thirdweb
quote: Standard zkEVMs use ZK proofs for scaling and verification of computation; their privacy aspects relate to inherent zero-knowledge proof mechanisms used for scalability rather than transaction confidentiality features.
